clue.text: Merchandise carried by these dancing couples, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words found here trade their beginnings

parts.note: bopping is lively dancing
shags, as British slang for acts of sex, are couplings; here used loosely for couples

explanation.surface: A ballroom-dancing pair seem to be carrying goods, in a deliberately naughty Spoonerism.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the B of BOPPING with the SH of SHAGS gives the answer. 'Shag' is British slang for sex, which the setter is enjoying here.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers carry their purchased goods home in sacks of this kind, so the clue describes their purpose.

clue.text: Cunning is not important in conversation

indicators.note: words spoken in conversation are heard, not seen, so the clue wants a word sounding like another

parts.note: slight means minor or not important

explanation.surface: A remark that cleverness counts for little when people are talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is skill in deception, as in sleight of hand, so it is a noun for cunning or craft.

clue.text: Extra dissertation nearly given degree, one gathers

indicators.note: one word gathers others when it collects them inside itself
nearly means stopping one letter short of the full word

parts.note: a thesis is a long academic dissertation

explanation.surface: A student's nearly finished dissertation earns them a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathers' is easy to read as the definition's verb, but it is the container signal around the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done as a sideline is an additional thing, so the phrase means an extra.

clue.text: Food scrap a starveling wraps

indicators.note: the words scrap a starveling wrap up the letters needed, which sit inside them

explanation.surface: A starving person wraps up any scrap of food they find.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti and macaroni are Italian staples, an everyday example of food.

clue.text: Mister Blue-Rinse gets a makeover

indicators.note: a makeover remodels something completely, so the letters of the hair treatment are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man with a blue-rinse hairdo is given a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like a title for a man, but it means something that produces a mist. A blue rinse is a hair tint associated with older ladies.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical device that turns liquid medicine into a fine spray to inhale is literally a thing that mists.

clue.text: British desire to whinge

parts.note: an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: A jibe that the British simply long to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To bitch is informal for complaining spitefully, a synonym of whinging.

clue.text: Better to walk at an easy pace in Greece

indicators.note: in places the stroll inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: GR is the international abbreviation for Greece

parts.words: to walk at an easy pace
parts.note: to amble is to walk slowly and easily

explanation.surface: Advice that strolling gently around Greece is preferable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as 'preferable' but is the noun: one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who places bets is a punter, so the noun one who bets fits.

clue.text: Stevie Nicks is such a striking performer

definitions.text: Stevie Nicks is such a striking performer

parts.words: Stevie Nicks is such a striking performer
parts.note: the Fleetwood Mac singer is famous for shaking and striking a jingling hand percussion instrument on stage; striking means hitting, not impressive

explanation.surface: Praise for the Fleetwood Mac singer as a dazzling stage presence.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays the jingling hand drum strikes it; Stevie Nicks often played one on stage.

clue.text: Negotiator's intelligence evident in vacuous account

indicators.note: the information is seen to sit within the emptied word
vacuous means empty, so only the outside letters of account are kept

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or intelligence

explanation.surface: A negotiator's insight shows in an empty report.
explanation.definitionFit: A representative who bargains for a client, such as a sports or literary representative, is a negotiator.

clue.text: Very small boat with music for twisting

indicators.note: the letters are offered up for twisting into a new order

explanation.surface: A tiny boat comes with music to dance the twist to.
explanation.definitionFit: Particles smaller than an atom, like electrons, are extremely tiny, so the term means very small.

clue.text: Uses sex in commercial arrangement

parts.note: customs are habitual uses or practices
union is a polite word for sexual intercourse

explanation.surface: Sex is used to sell in some business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade bloc removing tariffs among its members, such as the EU's, is a commercial agreement.

clue.text: Bother — shaking lager left nothing

parts.note: to bug someone is to bother them

indicators.note: shaking the drink jumbles its letters

explanation.surface: Someone shaking a can of lager has left none worth drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The British slang phrase means absolutely nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: This vulgar British idiom means not a thing at all, so it equals nothing.

clue.text: Stops key opening unoccupied houses

indicators.note: the key goes into the gap opened up in the emptied houses
unoccupied houses are empty, so only the outer letters survive

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Using a key to open empty houses is prevented.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt is to come to a standstill, so halts is a verb meaning stops.

clue.text: Setting free wobbly tiny gnu

indicators.note: wobbly signals that the letters are unstable and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Releasing a tottering little wildebeest from its tether.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfastening the knots of a rope releases what was bound, so it is setting free.

clue.text: Advances in age and death's all over the place

indicators.note: scattered all over the place, the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: In old age, death advances everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull ahead is to make progress, so the phrase means advances.

clue.text: Lively piece so describes that woman in Czech Republic

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so so encircles the rest
in places the pronoun inside the country code

parts.note: CZ is the international code for the Czech Republic
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A lively musical piece describes a woman in the Czech Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful, quick movement in a symphony or sonata is a lively piece of music.

clue.text: Racy type hides underwear at start of romance, one gathers

indicators.note: one creature hides the garment inside itself

parts.note: a hare is a fast, racing animal, a racy type
a vest is an undergarment in British usage

indicators.note: the start of romance means its first letter

explanation.surface: A saucy character hides her lingerie as romance begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racy type' suggests someone risqué, but means a speedy runner. In Britain a vest is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or machine that reaps the crop collects it, so it is one who gathers.

clue.text: Check out return of fungus within this month

indicators.note: within places the turned fungus inside the abbreviation for the month

parts.note: inst. (instant) is an old commercial abbreviation for this month

indicators.note: return means the fungus is read backwards

parts.note: a cep is an edible mushroom, a porcini

explanation.surface: Check out the fungus that comes back this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST, short for 'instant', is old business-letter usage for the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something closely is to check it out, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Mug American leaving penetrable place in Japan

parts.note: a sap is a mug, a gullible fool

indicators.note: leaving means the American letters depart from the word

parts.note: porous means letting liquid through, so penetrable

explanation.surface: A gullible American quits some vulnerable spot in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a major city on the Japanese island of Hokkaido, famous for its beer.

clue.text: Half-seriously into wines, mugs up again

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes into the wines

parts.note: reds are red wines

indicators.note: half of the synonym is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: really can mean seriously, as in 'really?'

explanation.surface: Someone half-seriously getting into wine studies the subject again.
explanation.walkthrough: The halving applies to a synonym of 'seriously', not to the printed word. 'Mugs up' is British slang for studies.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is British slang for studying hard, and going over a text again is revising it.

clue.text: Perhaps OPEC president has yen for cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: Emmanuel Macron is the French president
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: An oil cartel's president has a yearning to go cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cycling' moves the M of MACRONY from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: OPEC is built from the initial letters of its full name, an example of an abbreviation of that kind.

clue.text: Content to disclaim pelvic thrust

indicators.note: the content of the words, what they hold within, supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Someone happy to deny any pelvic thrusting.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive forward with force is to propel or push, as a verb thrust.

clue.text: Unlimited traditional beverage

indicators.note: without its limits, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: classic means traditional or time-honoured

explanation.surface: A traditional drink offered in unlimited quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Indian yogurt-based drink, a beverage.

clue.text: Inclination to decrease support for construction

parts.note: an angle is a slope or inclination
read as de-crease, to remove creases, which is to iron

explanation.surface: A tendency to cut back on support for a building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to decrease' looks like 'to reduce', but is split as de-crease: to iron.
explanation.definitionFit: L-shaped metal sections are used as structural support in building work.

clue.text: Oddly globular container for Dutch cheese

indicators.note: the selected letters act as a container for the Dutch abbreviation
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of globular

explanation.surface: A round container holds Dutch cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is also the setter's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous mild yellow cheese from the Netherlands.

clue.text: French artist after a bit of training as bottom drawer

indicators.note: the painter's name comes after that letter
a bit of training is just its first letter

parts.note: Henri Rousseau was a French painter

explanation.surface: A French painter works as a bottom drawer after some training.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottom drawer is British for the linen and clothes a woman collects before marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen for married life is called a bottom drawer in Britain.

clue.text: Announcing tea dance?

definitions.meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter T is announced with this code word

explanation.surface: An invitation to a tea dance being announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea' is the letter T, spoken in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: This is both the radio code word for T and a passionate Latin ballroom dance.

clue.text: Wandering goliard with magic plan

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places and form a new order

explanation.surface: A wandering medieval poet with a magical scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: A goliard was a wandering student poet of the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart setting out logical operations is a schematic plan of reasoning.
